rows.annotation: MurR/RpiR-family DNA-binding transcriptional regulator associated with amino sugar utilization.
rows.evidence: Query InterProScan identifies an N-terminal RpiR helix-turn-helix domain and C-terminal SIS domain. The 100%-identity STRING homolog ybbH associates strongly with murQ (963) and a PTS sugar transporter (923), supporting amino sugar utilization context. Distant Shewanella homologs show strong beneficial disruption phenotypes on NAG, but their broad phenotypes do not establish the query's effector, regulatory targets, or regulatory direction.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier A is supported by convergence of query-specific regulatory domains, the identical STRING homolog's sugar-utilization associations, and substrate-linked fitness evidence. Literature homologs support transcriptional regulation but provide no direct biochemical characterization of query-specific ligand binding; no cofitness or direct target-binding data are supplied. A specific HexR assignment or N-acetylmuramic acid-specific repressor annotation is unsupported because distant homolog contexts and network associations do not establish those identities or regulatory mechanisms.

PROTEIN SEQUENCE ORIGINATES FROM BACTERIA: Bacillus subtilis
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 40.70
Homolog originates from: Listeria monocytogenes
Evidence type: comparative
This gene encodes a family transcriptional regulator. It was identified as one of 28 genes exclusive to lineage I strains based on RPKM analysis [FIG:F5, Table 2].
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 33.50
Homolog originates from: Yersinia enterocolitica subsp. enterocolitica 8081
Evidence type: comparative
This gene is identified as part of the ycoR locus in Y. enterocolitica 8081. Sequence comparison between strain 8081 and strain 90/54 shows that YE1025 remains intact in both strains, despite the absence of ycoR in the 90/54 strain.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 32.10
Homolog originates from: Clostridium difficile 630
Evidence type: experimental
The authors identified that the transcription of this gene, which encodes a transcriptional regulator of the RpiR family, is driven by two internal promoters located inside the upstream gene CD3045.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 32.00
Homolog originates from: Burkholderia pseudomallei K96243
Evidence type: experimental
This putative regulatory protein was identified as a sigmaE-dependent oxidative-stress-responsive gene, showing increased expression under oxidative stress in the wild type and decreased expression in the sigmaE mutant.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 31.60
Homolog originates from: Aeromonas hydrophila
Evidence type: comparative
Identified as a gene involved in a specific metabolic pathway utilizing sialic acid; the presence of this pathway in HX-3 is used to suggest the strain may exhibit less virulence than some clinical isolates.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 31.50
Homolog originates from: Caldicellulosiruptor bescii DSM 6725
Evidence type: comparative
This gene is identified as a transcriptional regulator belonging to a hypothetical carbohydrate utilization (CU) pathway for oligosaccharides [Table 1]. It is part of a hypothetical CU gene locus (Athe_1993-97) where it is predicted to function as the regulator for the associated genes [Table 1].
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 31.50
Homolog originates from: Neisseria meningitidis MC58
Evidence type: experimental
This RpiR/YebK/YfhH family protein (orthologue of HexR) was targeted for knockout to test its role in Bns1 regulation. Northern blot analysis of the hexR null mutant showed that Bns1 is regulated as in the wild type, indicating NMB1389 does not regulate Bns1.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 31.50
Homolog originates from: Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2)
Evidence type: experimental
This transcriptional regulator showed significant differences in abundance between culture types, being down-regulated in MII in solid cultures (log2 = -1.4) and liquid cultures (log2 = -0.2).
[[END SUMMARY]]

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 25 (in 16 genera)
Query organism: Bacillus subtilis
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 25 (15 genera other than Bacillus)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 30.3-84.5
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
